structured_output.what_is_happening: This is a late clone riding a real viral story. On Sept 22, 2026, the family of Avery "The Poké Kid", a 12-year-old Pokémon creator who died of cancer, posted his final pack opening. In it he called for "last pack magic" and pulled a Jirachi SIR. Dexerto and others covered it, and the card's artist reacted publicly. At least 10 Solana tokens named "Last pack magic / JIRACHI" were launched off it, plus some on Ethereum. The earliest active one, HMD6… (created ~11:01 UTC, paired with CARDS, peaked around $580k), is now falling (-16% h1). This token (Qtj…) was created at 12:35 UTC, directly as a PumpSwap pool rather than through a bonding-curve graduation (migrated_unix=0). Its liquidity ($129k) is larger than its market cap ($105k). Its description is copied from a StonkFun launch and its image is duplicated 10 times. It shows $4M of volume in 40 minutes (30x turnover) from 2,048 unique buyers but only 56 unique sellers, who made about 2,758 sells. GMGN flags 49 bundler wallets holding 26% of top-trader volume. LP is 0% locked/burned, and RugCheck flags it as danger.

narrative.description: A tragic, emotional viral moment: a dying child's final Pokémon pull (a Jirachi SIR, 'last pack magic') during the Pokémon 30th anniversary. It is real, current, and covered by mainstream gaming and entertainment media.
narrative.why_spreading: Heartfelt Pokémon-community virality, amplified by Dexerto and the card artist's tearful reaction. Crypto degens farm this kind of news. The event itself is about 2 days old, and the first token peaked hours ago. A coin built on a child's death also risks backlash.

token_connection.why_this_token: None beyond the copied name and metadata. It links to Dexerto's tweet and StonkFun's Telegram, not to any community of its own. It is a later clone, launched about 1.5h after the first.
token_connection.competing_tokens: HMD6LV9h… (earliest active, $480k, CARDS pair, now declining); 8viD3J…/GamYh… (each shows ~$1.4M liquidity with zero volume, suspicious); an ETH Uniswap clone (0x0EA8…, +714% h1); at least 6 more small Solana clones.

authenticity.evidence: 2,048 unique buyers against only 56 unique sellers, who made ~2,758 sells, looks like a volume/holder bot plus a handful of seller wallets. The 30x h1 turnover suggests wash trading. GMGN flags 49 bundlers with 26% bundler share. The dev created the PumpSwap pool directly with unlocked LP. Metadata and image are copied. GMGN shows only 3 page visits despite $4M volume, so real attention is minimal.
authenticity.uncertainty: Some of the buyers could be real people chasing the narrative. The sell-side counts could partly reflect aggregator routing.

structural_risks: LP 0% burned/locked; the creator-supplied pool can be pulled at any moment
Liquidity is larger than market cap, which fits a dev-seeded pool set up to farm buyers
Only 56 sellers vs 2,048 buyers suggests bot-driven, fake demand
Many same-name clones splitting attention; the canonical token is already fading

structured_output.counterargument: The story is real, emotional and still spreading, and Pokémon's 30th anniversary gives it a mainstream audience. The token has deep liquidity and fixed authorities, it is still printing +7-10% per 5 minutes, and the canonical token peaked near $580k. A move from $105k to $210k is well within the range this narrative has already shown. If the deployer keeps the wash volume going to attract trending traffic, a 2x could happen before any pull.
unknowns: Whether the deployer's LP position is the whole pool and when it will be pulled
Real X discussion of this particular contract (X poorly indexed)
Whether the buyer count comes from a holder bot
Why two clones show ~$1.4M liquidity with zero volume

source_coverage.notes: X search found the Dexerto post about the event and a lore reply, but nothing on this contract. News coverage of the event is real (Dexerto, Yahoo, Player.one). The project site/Telegram is just the StonkFun launchpad. There is no Reddit coin discussion. DexScreener search confirms many clones. The Telegram listed is StonkFun's generic channel, so no private or project Telegram or Discord was checked.

structured_output.thesis: The narrative is real, but this token is a non-canonical late clone. Its pool was seeded directly by the deployer with unlocked LP, and its buy flow looks bot-driven (2,048 buyers vs 56 sellers, 30x turnover, 49 bundlers). The most likely outcome is a liquidity pull or a bleed-out, not a 2x from $105k.
